misconceptions.statement: All vitamins dissolve in water, so all can be washed out in cooking.
misconceptions.why: Students generalise from vitamin C and B being in fruit juices and soups.
misconceptions.fix: Vitamins A, D, E and K dissolve in fat, not water. Only B and C dissolve in water.

probe.question: Which vitamin is NOT easily lost into water when vegetables are boiled: vitamin A or vitamin C?
probe.wrong_answer: Both are lost equally because vitamins dissolve in water.

misconceptions.root_belief: what is true of some is true of all

misconceptions.statement: Vitamin B and vitamin C are the same vitamin.
misconceptions.why: Both are water-soluble and common in 'healthy food', and letters sound alike.
misconceptions.fix: B and C are different vitamins with different jobs and sources. Lack of B1 causes beriberi, lack of C causes scurvy.

probe.question: Will eating whole grains cure scurvy?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because grains have vitamins like B and C.

misconceptions.statement: Only oranges and lemons have vitamin C.
misconceptions.why: Textbooks and ads link vitamin C mainly with oranges.
misconceptions.fix: Amla, guava, tomato and many other fruits and vegetables also have vitamin C. Amla has more than oranges.

probe.question: Name a cheap Indian fruit rich in vitamin C other than citrus.
probe.wrong_answer: There is none; only oranges and lemons.

misconceptions.root_belief: one famous example is the only example

misconceptions.statement: Only sour-tasting foods contain vitamin C.
misconceptions.why: Lemon, amla and tamarind are sour, so taste seems the sign.
misconceptions.fix: Taste does not decide the vitamin. Some vitamin C foods like cabbage, green chilli and potato are not sour.

probe.question: Does sweet-tasting papaya or non-sour green chilli contain vitamin C?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because they are not sour.

misconceptions.root_belief: a visible property shows what is inside

misconceptions.statement: Carrots make eyesight perfect, so eating many carrots cures all eye problems.
misconceptions.why: Common sayings say carrots are good for eyes.
misconceptions.fix: Carrots give vitamin A which prevents night blindness. They do not cure other eye problems like needing spectacles.

probe.question: A child needs spectacles for blurred distant vision. Will eating carrots remove the need?
